events.title: Church defines effective calculability with lambda calculus
events.summary: Alonzo Church's April 1936 paper in the American Journal of Mathematics used lambda calculus to prove the Entscheidungsproblem unsolvable — the same year Turing published his machine model.
events.about: Church's lambda calculus became the theoretical basis for Lisp, functional programming, and type theory. Together with Turing's 1936 work, it established the Church–Turing thesis: anything effectively computable can be computed by these equivalent models.

narrative.whyChosen: Lambda calculus is one of two independent 1936 definitions of computation.
narrative.whyImportant: It linked logic to programming language design decades before computers were widespread.
narrative.problemSolved: Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem asked for a general procedure to decide mathematical truth — Church proved no such procedure exists.
